question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluation in a BCC program?

options.A: Monitoring is done only by doctors, while evaluation is done by patients
options.B: Evaluation happens before the project starts, and monitoring never happens
options.C: There is no difference; both words mean exactly the same thing
options.D: Monitoring is ongoing during the project, while evaluation measures final impact

explanation: Think of monitoring as checking your progress while running the race, and evaluation as looking at your overall performance and medals when the race is finished. You've got this distinction down! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a non-probability sampling method?

options.A: Convenience sampling
options.B: Simple random sampling
options.C: Snowball sampling
options.D: Purposive sampling

explanation: Correct! Simple random sampling belongs to the probability family because it relies on pure chance, not convenience or choice. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h4)

question: Which of these is a key focus during Antenatal Care (ANC) visits in Nigerian clinics?

options.A: Treating chronic adult diabetes mellitus
options.B: Scheduling permanent surgical sterilization
options.C: Conducting forensic examinations for survivors of abuse
options.D: Screening for conditions like gestational hypertension

explanation: Great thinking! ANC visits give nurses a wonderful chance to monitor blood pressure and catch dangerous pregnancy complications early. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why are regular hearing tests important for workers in noisy industrial plants?

options.A: They detect early hearing loss before the damage becomes permanent
options.B: They make the factory machines run much more quietly
options.C: They prove that loud noise has no effect on human ears
options.D: They replace the need for wearing earplugs

explanation: Routine testing spots subtle hearing changes early, prompting better protection before deafness occurs. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of the cold chain system?

options.A: Transporting medical personnel safely to remote rural outposts
options.B: Preventing theft of expensive pharmaceutical supplies in storage
options.C: Freezing needles and syringes to sterilize them before use
options.D: Keeping vaccines at the correct temperature to preserve their potency

explanation: Biological vaccines are sensitive to heat and require strict temperature controls to remain effective against diseases. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h3)

question: A patient takes a drug that blocks beta-3 receptors in the bladder. What problem are they most likely to face?

options.A: Inability to ever relax the external urethral sphincter
options.B: Complete paralysis of the pudendal nerve
options.C: Difficulty storing urine due to premature detrusor contractions
options.D: Permanent numbness in the pelvic floor region

explanation: Beta-3 receptors help the bladder relax. If you block them, the bladder can't chill out properly, leading to sudden urges and trouble holding urine. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h3)

question: Which of these common grains naturally contains gluten?

options.A: Sorghum
options.B: Rice
options.C: Millet
options.D: Barley

explanation: Barley is one of the main grains that naturally contains gluten, along with wheat and rye. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h1)

question: A doctor asks if a pregnant woman can safely take a certain antibiotic. What is your best first step as the nurse?

options.A: Gather details on the patient's exact gestational age and kidney function
options.B: Immediately tell the doctor that all antibiotics are dangerous in pregnancy
options.C: Refuse to answer because prescribing is outside the nursing scope
options.D: Look up the generic name in a pocket drug guide without asking further details

explanation: You got it! Patient details like pregnancy stage and kidney health completely change how a drug is used, so always gather background info first. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T3#GNS215_U2_T3_h3)

question: How should a nurse respond when a client expresses fear that an IUD will cause permanent infertility?

options.A: Tell the client that her fears are irrational and insist she accepts the device anyway
options.B: Provide calm, evidence-based education explaining that fertility returns immediately upon IUD removal
options.C: Agree that permanent damage is common and suggest she avoids all birth control
options.D: Ignore the comment and document that the client refused all medical advice

explanation: Respectful nursing care involves correcting myths gently with factual information while supporting the client's ultimate autonomy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h6)

question: Why are helper T-cells considered the master coordinators of the immune system?

options.A: They physically swallow large bacteria and digest them inside stomach acid.
options.B: They create a hard physical barrier around damaged skin to stop bleeding.
options.C: They release chemical signals that activate both B-cells and other T-cells.
options.D: They turn into red blood cells when the body suffers from severe anemia.

explanation: Helper T-cells act like military commanders, sending chemical messages to rally both B-cells and other T-cells into action. [learn more](GST114_U4_T5#GST114_U4_T5_h5)

question: What is the most important assessment to do before giving a patient an anti-spasmodic drug?

options.A: Testing the patient's grip strength in both hands
options.B: Measuring the circumference of the patient's neck
options.C: Checking the patient's visual acuity using a reading chart
options.D: Evaluating bowel sounds and the nature of abdominal pain

explanation: You always want to know what their pain and tummy sounds are like *before* giving the drug so you can tell if it's safe and if it actually helps them. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T4#GNS223_U3_T4_h6)

question: What do we call inflammation of the middle layer of the eye, which includes the iris?

options.A: Keratitis
options.B: Conjunctivitis
options.C: Retinitis
options.D: Uveitis

explanation: You got it! Uveitis is inflammation of the uvea (the middle layer). It can cause a deep, aching pain and make the eyes very sensitive to light. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T4#GNS311_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why is tetanus considered infectious, but not strictly communicable?

options.A: It spreads through the air rather than direct contact.
options.B: It cannot be treated with any known medications.
options.C: It only affects animals and never human beings.
options.D: It enters the body from the environment and does not spread from person to person.

explanation: Think of it this way: tetanus spores live in the soil and get in through wounds. You cannot catch tetanus directly from a patient lying next to you in the ward! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T87#GNS214_U1_T87_h1)

question: In a reflex arc, which part carries the nerve impulse away from the central nervous system?

options.A: Integration center
options.B: Sensory neuron
options.C: Motor neuron
options.D: Receptor cell

explanation: Motor neurons act like the delivery team, carrying the processed action signal away from the spinal cord out to the muscles or glands to take action. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T16#GNS211_U3_T16_h5)

question: Which of these is a key part of active listening for a nurse leader?

options.A: Listening to understand concerns rather than just waiting to speak
options.B: Writing down every single word spoken without making eye contact
options.C: Interrupting the speaker frequently to correct minor grammar mistakes
options.D: Agreeing with every demand made by patients and staff members

explanation: Active listening means turning off your mental reply-generator and genuinely trying to see things from the other person's point of view. [learn more](GST321_U3_T4#GST321_U3_T4_h5)

question: What lab tests must a nurse check before giving cytotoxic drugs?

options.A: Stool cultures and routine lipid panels
options.B: Urinary calcium and serum protein counts
options.C: Blood glucose and thyroid hormone levels
options.D: Complete blood count and organ function tests

explanation: Wonderful! We always check blood counts and kidney/liver labs first to make sure the patient's body can safely handle the medicine. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T7#GNS215_U6_T7_h6)

question: What is a major difference between thoracic spinal nerves and the nerves in the neck or lower back?

options.A: Thoracic nerves only carry sensory information
options.B: Thoracic nerves do not connect to the spinal cord
options.C: Thoracic nerves do not form complex nerve plexuses
options.D: Thoracic nerves lack ventral roots

explanation: While other regions braid together into big webs (plexuses), thoracic nerves stay independent as clean, separate intercostal nerves between the ribs. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h6)

question: What is the difference between allocative efficiency and technical efficiency?

options.A: Allocative efficiency deals with staff salaries, while technical efficiency deals with building construction
options.B: Allocative efficiency only applies to private clinics, while technical efficiency applies to government hospitals
options.C: Allocative efficiency eliminates all waste, while technical efficiency increases patient satisfaction
options.D: Allocative efficiency focuses on funding the right mix of services, while technical efficiency focuses on producing services at the lowest cost

explanation: Allocative is choosing the *right* things to do for the community, while technical is doing those things with zero waste. [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h3)

question: What happens during catabolism in the human body?

options.A: Body fat is created from excess dietary sugars.
options.B: Complex molecules are broken down to release energy.
options.C: Simple amino acids are joined to form large muscles.
options.D: Nutrients are absorbed through the intestinal wall.

explanation: Catabolism tears big molecules down into smaller pieces to release quick energy for your body to use. You're mastering metabolism! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T001#GNS227_U1_T001_h6)

question: In community health, what does the term 'social stratification' mean?

options.A: The official administrative mapping done by the local government
options.B: The physical division of land into residential and industrial zones
options.C: The seasonal migration of farmers during the dry harvest period
options.D: The ranking of people into layers based on wealth, status, or power

explanation: Social stratification just means how society is layered into different groups based on wealth, influence, and social standing. Knowing this helps nurses spot who might be missing out on care. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T1#GNS124_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of HIV counselling?

options.A: To enable the client to cope with stress and make personal decisions
options.B: To force patients to reveal their status to family members immediately
options.C: To diagnose opportunistic infections without laboratory tests
options.D: To register patients for mandatory government employment schemes

explanation: HIV counselling provides a safe space for clients to process emotions and make informed choices about their health. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h1)

question: Why is eating a balanced diet important when managing chronic fatigue?

options.A: It stops the digestive system from producing inflammatory enzymes.
options.B: It eliminates the need for any physical rest during the day.
options.C: It prevents blood sugar swings that drain daily energy reserves.
options.D: It directly increases the number of red blood cells in the liver.

explanation: Exactly! Balanced meals keep blood sugar stable. Big sugar spikes and crashes only make fatigue worse, so steady food equals steady energy. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T3#GNS123_U3_T3_h7)

question: Why is routine urinalysis important during pregnancy checkups?

options.A: It checks for protein and sugar, which show kidney stress or diabetes
options.B: It measures the heartbeat of the unborn baby
options.C: It tells the nurse the exact weight of the placenta
options.D: It proves whether the mother is eating enough vegetables

explanation: Protein in urine can point to pre-eclampsia, while sugar can point to diabetes, both needing close management. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h5)

question: What is the main goal of placing the harvested skin sample into normal saline or water?

options.A: To sterilize the sample from any surface bacterial contamination
options.B: To encourage the microfilariae to emerge out into the fluid
options.C: To dissolve the tissue completely so only DNA remains
options.D: To preserve the tissue for permanent paraffin embedding

explanation: Spot on! The liquid tricks the live microfilariae into crawling right out of the skin snippet so we can spot them under the microscope. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T13#GNS213_U5_T13_h3)

question: What is a main purpose of a family planning referral?

options.A: To permanently punish clients who miss their clinic appointments
options.B: To reduce the total number of people using modern contraceptives
options.C: To transfer financial responsibility for drugs to the client
options.D: To connect clients with specialized care when needed

explanation: Referrals are primarily designed to link clients to the specific level of care required for their health status. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h2)

question: A rural health clinic has only two nurses on duty. Which staffing approach ensures the best care for the community?

options.A: Firing the nurses and hiring administrative clerks
options.B: Employing polyvalent nurses trained in multiple care areas
options.C: Restricting care strictly to adult male patients
options.D: Closing the clinic until a specialist doctor arrives

explanation: Spot on! Having polyvalent nurses means a small team can safely and confidently handle a wide variety of health needs in the community. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h8)

question: What should always be done before going to the market to buy food?

options.A: Buy all items in bulk quantities
options.B: Select the most expensive brands
options.C: Wait for foods to start spoiling
options.D: Create a planned menu and budget

explanation: Having a menu and budget prevents impulse buying and ensures you only purchase what is necessary and affordable. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h2)

question: What is the main reason governments place heavy taxes on tobacco and sugary drinks?

options.A: To completely ban all agricultural farming activities in rural farming communities
options.B: To fund the construction of large international airports in every state capital
options.C: To make healthcare workers richer through direct salary commission bonuses
options.D: To discourage consumption and lower the population's risk of developing NCDs

explanation: Spot on! When unhealthy items become more expensive, people tend to buy less of them, which helps lower community rates of lifestyle diseases. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h7)

question: What causes the area around an infected wound to swell up?

options.A: Rapid shrinking of local muscle fibers
options.B: Blockage of the main nearby artery
options.C: Fluid leaking out of blood vessels into the tissue
options.D: A buildup of dead red blood cells

explanation: Well done! When your body fights an infection, tiny blood vessels loosen up, letting fluid flow into the tissues and cause that puffy swelling. [learn more](GST114_U2_T4#GST114_U2_T4_h3)

question: A mum at a rural health post has been at 5 cm dilation for the last 6 hours. What should you do next?

options.A: Perform a routine discharge with instructions to return tomorrow
options.B: Encourage her to walk around the ward for two more hours
options.C: Arrange immediate emergency transfer to a higher facility
options.D: Administer an oral sedative to help her rest overnight

explanation: Safety first! A stuck cervix for six hours is a red flag for prolonged labour. She needs to be transferred quickly to a hospital where doctors can provide emergency care. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h3)

question: What is the main job of 'inclusion criteria' when setting up a nursing study?

options.A: To increase the financial cost of running the clinical trial for the hospital
options.B: To punish patients who refuse to take their prescribed routine medications
options.C: To list every single complication that happened during the hospital admission
options.D: To define the specific characteristics a participant must possess to join the study

explanation: Well done! Inclusion criteria act like a checklist of traits a person must have to qualify for your research. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T17#GNS224_U1_T17_h3)

question: What is a major environmental factor that increases mosquito breeding and malaria transmission?

options.A: High altitude mountain air with low oxygen levels
options.B: Dense forest canopies blocking all sunlight
options.C: Cool, dry winds blowing during the harmattan season
options.D: Stagnant pools of water after heavy rainfall

explanation: Female mosquitoes lay their eggs in standing water, making puddles and poorly drained areas primary breeding sites after rain. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h4)

question: Why are community health nurses often the first to spot developmental delays in children?

options.A: They perform all surgical procedures in the country
options.B: They interact with families regularly during home and clinic visits
options.C: They manage the national legal courts
options.D: They live in federal legislative offices

explanation: Because community health nurses visit homes and local clinics often, they are in the best position to notice early developmental milestones and red flags. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T7#GNS225_U5_T7_h5)

question: When should a nurse put on a disposable gown and gloves for contact precautions?

options.A: Immediately before leaving the isolation ward
options.B: Before entering the patient's room or care area
options.C: Only when performing open wound dressing changes
options.D: After touching contaminated hospital bed rails

explanation: Always gown and glove up *before* stepping into the room. That way, your clothes and hands stay clean right from the start. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h7)

question: What naturally happens to serum albumin levels when a patient's body goes through sudden inflammation?

options.A: They remain unchanged
options.B: They increase
options.C: They decrease
options.D: They fluctuate wildly

explanation: Albumin is known as a negative acute-phase reactant. When inflammation flares up, the liver slows down albumin production—good to keep in mind! [learn more](GNS227_U5_T005#GNS227_U5_T005_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe home environment practice for a patient with Parkinson's disease?

options.A: Ensuring hallways and stairwells have bright, even lighting
options.B: Installing secure grab bars in the bathroom and shower
options.C: Clearing pathways of electrical cords and clutter
options.D: Placing loose decorative throw rugs over slick tile floors

explanation: Watch out for loose rugs! Because Parkinson's patients often shuffle their feet, throw rugs are a major tripping hazard that should always be removed. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T4#GNS222_U4_T4_h7)

question: What is a major financial headache caused by unreliable public electricity in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Automatic shutdown of all nursing schools
options.B: Heavy financial expenditure on diesel generators
options.C: Immediate reduction in patient admission rates
options.D: Instant conversion of hospitals to digital clinics

explanation: Spot on! Hospitals have to spend a massive chunk of their budgets buying diesel just to keep emergency lights and life-saving machines running. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why are interactive methods like role-play preferred over lecturing for school health instruction?

options.A: They guarantee that students will never fall ill
options.B: They require no preparation from the classroom teacher
options.C: Children prefer reading long medical textbooks
options.D: They actively engage students and improve practical habits

explanation: Interactive learning helps students internalize concepts and apply them to real-life situations better than passive listening. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is the main goal of community programs that prevent child abuse?

options.A: Removing all children from high-risk neighborhoods
options.B: Strengthening families and reducing stress before crises occur
options.C: Punishing parents who fail to attend community meetings
options.D: Replacing social welfare agencies with nurse-led clinics

explanation: Good prevention programs give parents the tools, coping skills, and support they need before things ever reach a crisis point. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T24#GNS225_U5_T24_h8)

question: What is the primary goal of prescribing cholinesterase inhibitors for a patient with Alzheimer's disease?

options.A: To completely reverse the formation of brain plaques
options.B: To temporarily manage symptoms and support daily function
options.C: To cure the underlying disease process within a few weeks
options.D: To prevent the patient from ever experiencing depression

explanation: These medications help boost chemical messengers in the brain to slow down symptom worsening, but they do not cure or reverse the disease. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T2#GNS222_U4_T2_h4)

question: What primary farming challenge do mountainous regions usually face?

options.A: Absence of any sunlight during the year
options.B: Excessive flat land and too much rainfall
options.C: Constantly flooded river basins
options.D: Steep slopes and short growing seasons

explanation: High altitudes have rocky, steep land and shorter periods of warm weather, making it tough for crops to grow. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T022#GNS227_U2_T022_h2)

question: Why do sudden increases in food prices hurt low-income households much harder than wealthy households?

options.A: Low-income families consume fewer total calories than wealthy individuals
options.B: Low-income households spend a much larger share of their total income on basic food items
options.C: Wealthy households are legally prohibited from buying discounted grocery items
options.D: Grocery stores charge high-income earners extra taxes on all purchases

explanation: When food takes up most of a family's budget, even a slight price hike leaves them with little room to adjust. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h7)

question: What is the main health benefit of birth spacing for a mother?

options.A: Allows her body enough time to recover its strength and nutrients
options.B: Ensures all her children are the same gender
options.C: Guarantees she will never have morning sickness again
options.D: Eliminates the need for future antenatal care

explanation: Spot on! Proper spacing prevents maternal depletion and gets the mother's body ready for a healthy future pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h7)

question: What is the very first thing you must do if a patient shows signs of an idiosyncratic drug reaction?

options.A: Stop the medication immediately
options.B: Wait forty minutes to see if it passes
options.C: Give a double dose of antihistamines
options.D: Increase the intravenous fluid rate

explanation: Safety first! Always stop the trigger drug right away to keep things from getting worse. You're thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T7#GNS125_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is the primary function of the epiglottis during swallowing?

options.A: Filter bacteria out of incoming swallowed liquids
options.B: Produce saliva to break down solid food particles
options.C: Pump air directly into the upper respiratory tract
options.D: Cover the larynx to direct food into the esophagus

explanation: The epiglottis acts as a protective lid that folds over the windpipe when we swallow, keeping food out of the airway. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T7#GNS324_U6_T7_h1)

question: What is another popular name for the ductus deferens?

options.A: Urethral tube
options.B: Vas deferens
options.C: Ejaculatory canal
options.D: Seminiferous duct

explanation: You will hear clinical instructors and textbooks use 'ductus deferens' and 'vas deferens' interchangeably. They are the exact same tube! [learn more](GNS121_U4_T2#GNS121_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is one common drawback of giving medications through mucous membranes?

options.A: Guaranteed 100% absorption for every patient
options.B: Longer time to onset than oral tablets
options.C: Risk of local irritation and variable absorption
options.D: Elimination of the need for nurse verification

explanation: Tissues in the mouth, rectum, or eyes can sometimes get sore or irritated by potent drugs, and how fast they absorb can change depending on how moist or healthy the tissue is. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T15#GNS125_U3_T15_h6)

question: Which organ system uses hormones to regulate slow, long-term body processes?

options.A: The nervous system
options.B: The muscular system
options.C: The endocrine system
options.D: The respiratory system

explanation: Glands in the endocrine system secrete chemical messengers called hormones directly into the bloodstream to control distant target organs over time. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T9#GNS111_U1_T9_h3)

question: A rural primary health clinic lacks doctors and has very few nurses. What practical step can help improve teen health access?

options.A: Ban all adolescents from visiting the facility
options.B: Utilize task-shifting to train local health extension workers
options.C: Close the clinic until more doctors are hired from abroad
options.D: Charge extremely high fees to filter out patients

explanation: Spot on! Task-shifting lets us train community health workers to deliver basic adolescent care, bridging staff gaps in rural areas. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T17#GNS312_U3_T17_h8)

question: What is the most effective first step a nurse can suggest to help a patient cut down on hidden sugars?

options.A: Eating only raw vegetables for breakfast and lunch
options.B: Replacing sugary sodas and packaged fruit juices with plain water
options.C: Eliminating all complex carbohydrates from every meal
options.D: Switching from white table sugar to organic raw honey

explanation: Sugary drinks are the biggest source of hidden calories in most diets. Swapping them for water is the easiest and most powerful change a patient can make! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T012#GNS227_U4_T012_h5)

question: What is the primary cause of acute shock immediately following FGM?

options.A: Long-term infertility
options.B: Chronic urinary tract infection
options.C: Psychological anxiety and depression
options.D: Severe pain and massive hemorrhage

explanation: The crude and unanesthetized cutting of highly vascular genital tissue frequently causes heavy bleeding and overwhelming pain, leading to shock. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which fluid-filled cavity does the diencephalon surround?

options.A: The fourth ventricle near the pons
options.B: The lateral ventricles of the frontal lobes
options.C: The central canal of the spinal cord
options.D: The third cerebral ventricle

explanation: Spot on! The structures of the diencephalon form the walls and floor around the third ventricle to help circulate cerebrospinal fluid. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T19#GNS211_U3_T19_h1)

question: Which of these nursing actions is NOT a priority when caring for a patient having an acute sickle cell pain crisis?

options.A: Providing adequate hydration with intravenous fluids
options.B: Administering prescribed analgesics for pain relief
options.C: Administering supplemental oxygen if oxygen saturation is low
options.D: Administering scheduled doses of oral iron supplements

explanation: Iron pills won't help during a sickle cell crisis and could be harmful. The main goals during a crisis are keeping the patient well-hydrated, giving oxygen if needed, and managing their pain! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T14#GNS311_U2_T14_h8)

question: What is a main purpose of conducting a community diagnosis?

options.A: To provide extra funding for international medical research
options.B: To allocate limited healthcare resources where they are needed most
options.C: To replace the need for individual patient physical examinations
options.D: To increase the patient admission rates in private hospitals

explanation: Resources are always limited, so finding the highest priority problems ensures supplies and personnel go where they will do the most good. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h2)

question: A patient catches malaria after being bitten by an infected mosquito. How would you classify this transmission?

options.A: Direct contact transmission
options.B: Airborne transmission
options.C: Vector-borne transmission
options.D: Vehicle-borne transmission

explanation: Mosquitoes, ticks, and other living creatures that carry germs to us are called vectors. That makes this a classic vector-borne disease! [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h4)

question: What does it mean to put research results into 'context'?

options.A: Translating the research report into three different languages
options.B: Comparing new study findings with past literature and clinical realities
options.C: Destroying old textbooks so staff only read the newest articles
options.D: Increasing the hospital budget to match the research costs

explanation: Contextualization just means looking at how new findings fit alongside existing science and whether they make sense on a busy ward. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T3#GNS224_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why is patting the perineal skin dry just as important as washing it?

options.A: Wet skin makes it impossible to apply a clean hospital gown
options.B: Leaving moisture behind fosters bacterial growth and skin breakdown
options.C: Rough rubbing removes the patient's natural body hair
options.D: Moisture attracts insects into the hospital room

explanation: Germs love warm, wet places. Taking that extra second to pat the area completely dry is a simple step that keeps skin strong and healthy. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T8#GNS112_U5_T8_h5)

question: Why is an oscillating cast saw safe against human skin during cast removal?

options.A: The saw is powered by low-voltage batteries that stop when touching skin
options.B: The metal blade is coated with a special chemical that repels human tissue
options.C: The blade vibrates back and forth instead of spinning in a continuous circle
options.D: The vibration creates a cooling effect that hardens the skin temporarily

explanation: The oscillating (back-and-forth) motion cuts right through hard plaster, but just bounces safely off soft, stretchy skin. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h8)

question: When studying how patients cope with long-term illness, why are interviews often better than rigid surveys?

options.A: Interviews allow participants to explain things in their own words
options.B: Surveys are too expensive to print out in hospital wards
options.C: Interviews do not require any ethical review board approval
options.D: Surveys only work when patients are unconscious

explanation: Spot on! People aren't checkboxes. Letting patients talk freely gives you rich insights that a standard survey would completely miss. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h1)

question: What was the main goal of introducing workers' compensation laws?

options.A: To fund free medical schools for aspiring occupational health nurses
options.B: To allow employers to fire injured workers immediately without paying severance
options.C: To punish factory owners by throwing them in prison for safety violations

question: Why does the body keep the testes in the scrotum, slightly cooler than the rest of the body?

question: Why is active participation of the patient and family considered a core CBR principle?

question: Why is it important for psychiatric nurses to ask patients about alternative therapies?

question: What is the main goal of community health nurses when it comes to burn safety?

question: In community health, why do leaders rely more on personal trust than strict job titles?

question: Why is writing up your transport documentation right after a medevac mission so important?

options.C: Safe, Meaningful, Accessible, Rapid, Tender
options.D: Systematic, Manual, Analytical, Routine, Tested

explanation: Spot on! SMART goals help nurses and patients set clear, realistic, and trackable targets for recovery. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the primary male sex hormone responsible for secondary sex characteristics?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Testosterone
options.D: Aldosterone

explanation: Testosterone is made mainly by the testes. It drives male reproductive development, muscle building, and masculine physical traits. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T5#GNS211_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why does the surface of the brain have so many folds and grooves?

options.A: To improve the circulation of cerebrospinal fluid
options.B: To increase the surface area for more neurons
options.C: To separate the left and right sides of the body
options.D: To absorb physical shock from head injuries

explanation: Folding packs a massive amount of brain power into a small space, giving us room for lots of nerve cells! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h2)

question: Which of these is a very common nursing diagnosis for a patient struggling with a severe phobia?

options.A: Impaired Gas Exchange
options.B: Deficient Fluid Volume
options.C: Risk for Infection
options.D: Ineffective Coping

explanation: Because phobias rely heavily on avoidance rather than healthy problem-solving, 'Ineffective Coping' fits right in your care plan. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T6#GNS314_U2_T6_h6)

question: A patient says they drink strong cough syrup containing codeine every day just to chill and relax. What is happening here?

options.A: Proper management of a chronic upper respiratory infection
options.B: Substance misuse and potential psychological dependence
options.C: An effective strategy to build natural immunity against colds
options.D: A harmless alternative to sleeping pills

explanation: Well done! Using codeine-lacking syrups just for a high or relaxation leads straight down the road to substance abuse and addiction. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h2)

question: Your CBI patient has bright red drainage and is crying out with severe lower tummy cramps. What's the most likely issue?

options.A: Rapid healing of the surgical wound inside the bladder
options.B: A blocked catheter trapping fluid and blood clots
options.C: A normal reaction to room-temperature saline solution
options.D: An allergic reaction to the antiseptic skin wipes

explanation: Think of it like a clogged sink: fluid keeps pouring in, but nowhere to go. This stretches the bladder and causes painful cramps. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T23#GNS212_U1_T23_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT part of a holistic palliative assessment?

options.A: Respecting cultural beliefs and family traditions
options.B: Strictly monitoring laboratory blood cell counts
options.C: Evaluating emotional and psychological well-being
options.D: Listening to spiritual and existential concerns

explanation: While lab results matter in acute care, palliative care is all about the human experience—feelings, culture, and spirit. It's much more than just numbers on a lab sheet! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which Nigerian agency leads national disease tracking and outbreak responses?

options.A: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC)
options.B: World Health Organization (WHO)
options.C: Federal Ministry of Information
options.D: National Primary Health Care Development Agency

explanation: Spot on! The NCDC is our frontline federal agency keeping watch over public health safety across Nigeria. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h4)

question: When a patient is prescribed both a bronchodilator and an inhaled corticosteroid, which one should they generally use first?

options.A: Whichever medication is closer to hand
options.B: The corticosteroid to coat the throat
options.C: The bronchodilator to open the airways
options.D: Neither, they must be mixed together first

explanation: Using the bronchodilator first opens up the air passages, allowing the subsequent corticosteroid to penetrate much deeper into the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h8)

question: Which of the following is a major objective of the Mother-Baby Package?

options.A: To reduce maternal, fetal, and newborn mortality rates
options.B: To increase the cost of maternity drugs in local clinics
options.C: To eliminate all traditional birth attendants completely
options.D: To transfer all pregnant women to tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: Exactly right! Every clinical guideline and care package ultimately aims to keep both mum and baby safe, healthy, and alive. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h2)

question: In the emergency ABCDE assessment check, what does the letter 'B' stand for?

options.A: Breathing
options.B: Blood pressure
options.C: Bone
options.D: Bleeding

explanation: Easy and correct! 'B' stands for Breathing. Checking chest movement is one of the very first things we do for any emergency patient. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T10#GNS112_U7_T10_h2)

question: What is the main benefit of sharing your final evaluation results with the community?

options.A: It stops all future health problems from ever returning
options.B: It legally forces every citizen to donate money to the clinic
options.C: It fosters transparency and helps everyone learn lessons for the future
options.D: It proves that the nursing staff made zero errors during the project

explanation: Sharing results builds trust and empowers the community to keep up the good work and learn what to improve next time. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T2#GNS124_U3_T2_h8)

question: Why is it smart to partner with existing groups like age-grades or church/mosque committees?

options.A: They are legally required to manage government health clinics
options.B: They provide a steady source of income for health workers
options.C: They already hold influence and command trust among members
options.D: They possess formal medical training recognized by the ministry

explanation: Spot on! Working through groups that people already belong to and trust makes it much easier to share important health messages. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h5)
